A black stone like a bean is found in the Nile; upon seeing it, dogs do not bark. You might carry a dog's tongue placed under your big toe inside your shoe, or if you carry a dried dog's heart with you, according to Sextus <note>Sextus Placitus, a 4th-century medical writer</note>, or a hare's hair or dung, according to Pliny. Or you might carry the severed tail of a young weasel on your foot, or give a dog a frog in a morsel of food; all these things serve to avoid the barking of dogs. Nigidius <note>Nigidius Figulus, a Roman scholar and associate of Cicero</note> says that dogs will flee the sight of one who pulls a tick from a pig and carries it for a little while. Oppian <note>A Greco-Roman poet who wrote on hunting and fishing</note> says:

> But if you carry a tiny piece cut from the skin of a hyena,
> Immediately the pups and fierce dogs will be struck
> With sharp terror; hereafter they will not bark at you
> As you walk, even if they barked before.

### How a dog may be unable to run.

If you smear its wings <note>likely referring to the "armpits" or joints of the legs in this context</note> with oil, it will be hindered in its course; it happens in this manner.

### That a hawk may be courageous.

You shall embolden the bird against its prey so that it attacks large birds. Moisten the meat it uses during hunting time with wine; or if it is a goshawk, give it a little vinegar. When you wish it to fly, give it three morsels of meat soaked in wine, or pour wine from your own mouth into the beak of a young pigeon <note>which is then fed to the hawk</note>, then let it fly. In this way:

### You will make partridges more combative,

If you give them branches of <term>adiantum</term> <gloss>maidenhair fern</gloss> in their food, according to Pliny; and

### Roosters become more combative,

By giving them garlic in their food just before they fight; for which reason, in Old Comedy <note>specifically referring to the plays of Aristophanes</note>, they were most wittily called <term>eskorodismenoi</term> <gloss>garlic-fed</gloss>, meaning those who are vehement and too inclined toward a fight.

### Lest a bird fly high,

Pluck the feathers of the tail which direct the course upward; thus it will fly below in a circle. If you wish:

### That a bird be unable to fly,

Cut the upper and lower nerves of the wing; it remains without further harm, yet the bird will not fly. In this way, they do not escape from aviaries.

<summary>This page provides folklore and practical methods for managing animals during hunting, including charms to silence barking dogs, techniques to embolden hawks and roosters, and ways to ground birds in aviaries.</summary>
<keywords>animal husbandry, hunting dogs, falconry, Oppian, Pliny, folk medicine, cockfighting, aviary management</keywords>

shines forth through piety, religion, prudence, and the worship and veneration of God, as if he perceived the truth with his own eyes through right reason. By the confidence of his belief, he stands as far above other men as the sun excels the rest of the stars by its light. For the sun itself illuminates the other stars not so much by the magnitude of its power as by its divinity and holiness. Believe that this sun, O Asclepius, is second to God, governing all other things and illuminating all worldly creatures, whether they possess a soul <note>original: "animantia"</note> or are inanimate. For if the world is a living being <note>original: "animal mundus"</note> that always lives—and was, and is, and shall be—nothing in the world is mortal. Since every part of a living being exists within the world itself, as if in one and the same eternally living animal, there is no place for mortality. Therefore, God must be most full of life and eternity himself, if it is necessary for him to live forever. Consequently, just as the world is eternal, so too is the sun the perpetual governor of living things, or the constant attendant and dispenser of their entire vitality. God is the eternal governor of the living beings and vital forces within the world, and he is the eternal dispenser of life itself. He distributed this life once through an eternal law, providing life to all living things in the manner I shall now describe.

<summary>Hermes explains that the sun acts as a secondary deity and governor that illuminates and sustains all life within the world. He argues that because the world is a single, eternally living being, nothing within it is truly mortal, and God serves as the eternal dispenser of life.</summary>
<keywords>Asclepius, Hermes Trismegistus, sun, divinity, world soul, eternity, governor of life, immortality, vital force, cosmic order</keywords>

At Megara, a certain rock produces the sound of a lute-player when struck with pebbles, so great is the power of Music. It <unclear>likewise</unclear> soothes the soul, lifts the mind, incites warriors to <unclear>war</unclear>, and <unclear>takes away</unclear> the labors and fatigue of individual tasks. It recalls those who have fallen and are in despair, and comforts travelers. And the <term>Arabes</term> <gloss>Arabs</gloss> say that camels carrying heavy loads are comforted by their singing drivers. In a similar way, those carrying heavy burdens sing, and by this, they are made capable and are relieved: for song produces delight and capability. It softens the angry, gladdens the sad and anxious, pacifies those in discord, tempers the madness of the <term>phrenetic</term> <gloss>those suffering from delirium or mental agitation</gloss>, and dissipates vain thoughts. Hence it is that <term>Democritus</term> and <term>Theophrastus</term> affirm that some diseases of the body and soul can be either cured or induced in this way. for the good is innate to Truth, along with life and light. No longer has the avenger <note>original: "uindex"; referring to the punishing or restrictive nature of the material vices</note> approached to go further. Indeed, all the avengers have been cast back by a certain sudden impulse. You have understood, my son, the manner of this **rebirth** <note>original: "regenerationis"</note>. When the **number ten** <note>original: "denario"; the decad, symbolizing perfection and the ten divine virtues</note> is present, the intellectual generation is complete, which rejects the **number twelve** <note>original: "duodenariū"; the dodecad, symbolizing the twelve zodiacal vices</note>. We have observed this from the generation itself. Therefore, whoever loses physical sensation because of the kindness of this generation, which is according to God, knows himself to be composed of divine things. Having been made unswerving, he rejoices with his whole mind in the divine power.

**TATIUS.** O father, I conceive this not by the sight of my eyes, but by the act of the mind, which is exercised through inward powers. I am in heaven; I am in the earth; in the water; in the air. I am in the animals; in the trees; in the body; before the body; and after the body. But I wish you would tell me this further: how are the avenging darknesses, twelve in number, repelled by the ten powers? By what means, Trismegistus?

**HERMES.** This tabernacle, O son, is constituted from the **zodiac circle** <note>original: "zodiaco circulo"</note>, which consists of that number twelve. The numbers are eleven; one is all-forming according to the ideas of nature, for the wandering and circuit of man. Thus, those avengers are in a certain way separated from one another, yet in their action they are in a certain way joined together. For example, recklessness is inseparable from wrath. Therefore, according to right reason, they are at a distance only insofar as they are repelled by the ten powers <note>original: "apotellatib9 decem"</note>, that is, by the number ten. The number ten, O son, is the parent of the soul. Indeed, Life

These are followed by the gods whose prince is <term>ousia</term> <gloss>essence or substance</gloss>. These sensible gods are alike in their dual origin, and they create all things through their sensible nature, each one illuminating his own work through the other. Jupiter is the <term>ousiarches</term> <gloss>ruler of essence</gloss> of the heaven, or whatever is understood by that name; for through the heaven, Jupiter provides life to all. The <term>ousiarches</term> of the sun is light; for the Good of light is infused into us through the solar orb. There are thirty-six <note>referring to the Decans of the zodiac</note> whose name is <term>Horoscopoi</term> <gloss>Markers of the Hour</gloss>, stars always fixed in the same place; their <term>ousiarches</term> or prince is the one they call <term>Pantomorphon</term> <gloss>The All-Formed</gloss> or <term>Omniform</term>, who creates diverse forms for diverse species. The seven spheres which are called "erratic" <note>the seven wandering planets</note> have their <term>ousiarchas</term>, that is, their own princes, whom they call Fortune or <term>Heimarmene</term> <gloss>Fate</gloss>. By these all things are changed by the law of nature with the firmest stability, varied by eternal agitation. The air, however, is the organ or the machine of all things, through which all things are made. Furthermore, there is a second <term>ousiarches</term> of this <note>the air</note>, providing mortal things to mortals and things similar to them. Since these things are thus arranged, moving from the bottom to the top, all things belonging to each other are naturally connected, so that mortal things are annexed to mortals and sensible things to sensibles. However, the height of governance obeys that supreme Lord, so that they are not many, but rather one. For since all things hang from one, and rather flow down from Him, when they are seen at a distance they are believed to be many and divided. But united they are one, or rather two: that from which all things are made, and He by whom they are made. That is, from the matter out of which they are made, and by the will of Him by whose nod other things are effected. ASCLEPIUS: What is this reasoning again, O Trismegistus? brought itself forth. Indeed, arsenic can truly in no way be fixed unless the operating artist recognizes its tinting spirit in equal measure. In this matter, all the philosophers have been asleep, fruitlessly attempting to produce something from it. Whoever, therefore, is ignorant of this spirit should have no hope of fixing it, nor of bestowing upon it the power by which it might acquire the perfection of transmutation. For this reason, I make it known to all that the whitening of which mention was made is derived from a false foundation; by it, copper is falsely whitened but not changed. The Sophists have mixed <term>Venus</term> <gloss>copper</gloss>, masked and painted in this manner, with twice as much <term>Luna</term> <gloss>silver</gloss>, and sold it to goldsmiths and coin-makers. Ultimately, they transformed themselves into counterfeiters—not only those who sold it, but even those who bought it. Some of the Sophists took red arsenic instead of white, and this itself resulted in a false art. For in whatever way it is prepared, it exhibits nothing but whiteness. Others proceeded further to common sulfur, which they cooked until it turned yellow with vinegar, lye, or the sharpest urines, day and night, until whiteness emerged. Afterward, they raised it from common salt and lime of eggs <note>calcium carbonate from crushed eggshells</note>; they cooked and sublimated it through sublimation, and this many times. Nevertheless, it remained always combustible, even though white. With it, however, they sought to fix raw mercury <unclear>…</unclear>

<summary>Paracelsus exposes the deceptive practices of "Sophists" who use arsenic and sulfur to create a surface whitening of copper to mimic silver. He warns that these chemical treatments do not achieve true transmutation and result in fraudulent metallurgy.</summary>

<keywords>arsenic, fixation, copper, silver, counterfeiters, sulfur, sublimation, mercury, alchemy, fraud</keywords>

Our material, however, is not bought from any shop, yet it is found in them daily, and merchants cast it out into the streets. It is sufficient, therefore, that it be found for free. But the material of our <term>lapis</term> <gloss>Stone</gloss> is compared to all those things with which the artisans labor: for our Stone is <term>sal nostrum</term> <gloss>our salt</gloss>, <term>Mercurius noster</term> <gloss>our Mercury</gloss>, <term>ærugo</term> <gloss>verdigris</gloss>, <term>halonitrum</term> <gloss>saltpeter</gloss>, <term>salmiacum</term> <gloss>sal ammoniac</gloss>, <term>Mars</term> <gloss>iron</gloss>, <term>sulphur</term> <gloss>sulfur</gloss>, and infinite other things of that kind, yet it is not dug out from wild and rustic mountains with hammers and other instruments. But only from our mountains and springs is our Stone extracted: in our <term>Salis-fonte</term> <gloss>Salt-spring</gloss> our <term>Sal</term> <gloss>Salt</gloss> is found: from our earth our metal, <term>Mercurius</term> <gloss>Mercury</gloss>, and <term>sulphur</term> <gloss>sulfur</gloss> is poured, and not from wild, foreign, and rustic mountains; all of which the artisans do not understand, nor can they believe or comprehend. For the Lord has darkened and stopped up their senses, for which reason they used these things otherwise than they ought to have been, and missed the mark entirely. Nevertheless, they persisted in that contrary sense and followed their own stubborn heads; for instance, while they ought to have <term>destillare</term> <gloss>distilled</gloss> gently, they instead <term>sublimarunt</term> <gloss>sublimated</gloss> there with a strong fire, scorched with <term>aquas fortes</term> <gloss>strong waters/acids</gloss>, and immediately burned the operation of nature and its substances, reducing them to nothing. Also, when they should have <term>solvere</term> <gloss>dissolved</gloss>, they <term>coagularunt</term> <gloss>coagulated</gloss> there, and again, like men unskilled in things, they handled the matter unskillfully, fell into doubt, and with lying words repeatedly claimed the art was not true, but false. In this, however, they themselves are deservedly lying: for their own ignorance shamefully deceived them, which is to be imputed to their own obscure and misty cunning, while, according to their own dark understanding, they interpreted words differently than they sounded. For example, when the Philosophers spoke of <term>calcionando</term> <gloss>calcining</gloss> (which they call grinding), then those unskilled <term>Philosophastri</term> <gloss>pretender-philosophers</gloss> understood it as burning, and reduced the things entirely to ashes, so that nothing could be fashioned from them. Also, when the Philosophers <term>solvunt</term> <gloss>dissolve</gloss> or transmute into water, then those <term>nasutuli</term> <gloss>know-it-alls/smug ones</gloss> burned nature with <term>forti aqua</term> <gloss>strong water</gloss>, and with that same water, which has no

requires a moderation of the fire, and a succession of its increase little by little, with caution, until it is fixed in its own <term>calx</term> <gloss>powdered oxide</gloss>, so that it may not easily return into a body <note>revert to its metallic state</note>, so that a greater fire can be administered to it for the perfection of its <term>calx</term>. Similarly, let it not happen that he errs regarding <term>Jupiter</term> <gloss>Tin</gloss>, because of the difficulty of its reduction; as when he has placed its <term>calx</term> for reduction, it may happen to him that it does not reduce, but he finds it in its former disposition or turned into glass, and he judges its reduction impossible. For we say that if he does not apply a great fire in the reduction of <term>Jupiter</term>, it will not reduce. If, however, he applies a great one, it does not necessarily happen that he reduces it, but it is possible to turn it into <term>vitrification</term> <gloss>the process of turning into glass</gloss>. And this is because <term>Jupiter</term> <margin>am ta</margin> in the depths of its nature has a fugitive substance of <term>argentum vivum</term> <gloss>quicksilver or mercury</gloss> enclosed. Which, if it endures a long delay in the fire, will flee, and leave the body deprived of humidity, so that it is found to be turned into something more suited for vitrification than for the fusion of a metallic body. For everything deprived of its own humidity gives no fusion except a vitrifying one. Therefore, it is necessarily left that he should hasten to reduce it quickly with a most rapid impetus of fire. Otherwise it is not reduced. Let him therefore practice this, and he shall know.

The <gloss>second</gloss> mode of calcination of these two bodies <gloss>Saturn and Jupiter</gloss> <margin>85, 6</margin>, which is perfected by the sharpness of salt, is that a quantity of salt be thrown upon their surface, quantity after quantity very often during its fusion, and they should be mixed with much stirring by an iron rod over the fire, until they are turned into ash through the mixing of the salt. <margin>wooden rod. boil here page 57, 14.</margin> And afterwards, by the same method of perfection, their <term>calx</term> may be perfected, with its own considerations. But in this there is also a difference in the calcination of these two bodies. Because <term>plumbum</term> <gloss>Lead</gloss> is converted to powder more easily than <term>Jupiter</term> <gloss>Tin</gloss> from the first labors of calcination; yet its <term>calx</term> is not perfected more easily than that of <term>Jupiter</term>. The cause of this depends on the fact that <term>Saturn</term> <gloss>Lead</gloss> has a more fixed humidity than <term>Jupiter</term>.

829. Since religion resides in the highest parts of a person, and from those highest parts the lower things live and shine, and because **Mohammed** <note>original: "Mahumedes"</note> is present in their minds along with their religion, some "Mohammed" is always placed in their sight. So that they may turn their faces toward the East, over which the Lord resides, he is placed below the Christian Center <note>original: "Meditullium Christianum"</note>. This is not the original Mohammed who wrote the **Koran** <note>original: "Alcoranum"</note>, but another who performs his office; nor is it always the same person, for he is changed. Once it was a man from **Saxony** who, having been captured by the **Algerians**, became a **Mohammedan** <note>Muslim</note>. Because he had also been a Christian, he was occasionally moved to speak with them about the Lord, saying that He was not the son of Joseph, but the Son of God Himself. Other men succeeded this Mohammed afterward. In the place where that representative Mohammed has his seat, a fire appears like torches so that he may be known; but that fire is not visible to anyone other than the Mohammedans.

830. The actual Mohammed who wrote the Koran does not come into view today. I was told that in the earliest times he presided over them, but because he wished to rule over everything of their religion as a God, he was ejected from his seat—which he held beneath the Roman Catholics—and sent down to the right side near the south. Once, when a certain society of Mohammedans was incited by malicious spirits to acknowledge Mohammed as God, Mohammed was raised up from the lower earth and shown to them to settle the sedition; I saw him then as well. He appeared similar to corporeal spirits who have no interior perception, with a face bordering on black, and I heard him speaking these words: *I am your Mohammed*; and soon he seemed to sink back down.

831. The Mohammedans are hostile to Christians primarily because of the belief in three Divine Persons, and the resulting worship of three Gods and three Creators; and they are hostile to the Roman Catholics additionally because of their kneeling before images. For this reason, they call the latter idolaters and the former fanatics, saying that they make a three-headed God, and that they say "one" but mutter "three," and consequently they split apart Omnipotence, making three out of the one and only. They say Christians are like **Fauns** with three horns, one for each God, and yet three for one, and that they thus pray, thus sing, and thus sound from their pulpits.

832. Like all nations who acknowledge one God, love what is just, and do good from a religious motive, the Mohammedans have their own Heaven, but it is outside the Christian one. The Mohammedan Heaven is divided into two: in the lower one they live honestly with many wives, but from there no others are elevated into the higher Heaven than those who renounce concubines and acknowledge the Lord as our Savior, and at the same time acknowledge His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think that God the Father and our Lord are one, but that it is possible for them to believe that He rules over the Heavens and Hells because He is the Son of God the Father. This is the faith among them through which the Lord grants them ascent into the higher Heaven.

833. That the Mohammedan religion is accepted by more kingdoms than the Christian religion can be a scandal <note>a cause for stumbling or doubt</note> to those who think about Divine Providence and at the same time believe that no one can be saved except those born Christian. But the Mohammedan religion is not a scandal to those who believe that all things belong to Divine Providence; these people inquire into its purpose, and they find it. It consists in this: that the Mohammedan religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the Wisest of all, and also as the Son of God. But because they have made only the Koran the book of their religion, and consequently Mohammed (who wrote it) resides in their thoughts and they follow him with some worship, they think little about our Lord. To fully understand that this religion was raised up by the Divine Providence of the Lord to destroy the idolatries of many nations, it will be described in some order; but first, concerning the origin of idolatries. plainly, the greatest part of diseases coming from celestial Influence and from the Astral Impression of the Firmament of the Greater World <note>the macrocosm or universe</note> do not wish to be cured with indiscriminate remedies, such as through the <term>Arcana</term> <gloss>secret essences</gloss> of herbs, minerals, or metals. Instead, the cure should be established through Astronomical Influence with at least those things which have an analogy to the greater and lesser world <note>the human body as microcosm</note>. In these things, there is a true Magnetic force of the Firmament and a Celestial Impression for resisting diseases from the Firmament of the greater and lesser world, as appears in Persicaria <note>smartweed</note>, Greater Solidago <note>goldenrod</note>, Dracunculus <note>dragonwort</note>, and Greater Symphytum <note>comfrey</note>.

If a disease or pain has been inflicted Supernaturally through incantation or a Magic Impression of the Ascendants, then the effort of the first three ways of healing is useless. Instead, according to Paracelsus, one must proceed Magically and Supernaturally, and the evil must be repelled in the same manner by which it was inflicted. Otherwise, in the said Simples <note>medicinal herbs</note> there is an Influential attractiveness, and they cure all things according to Divine ordination Magically, Astronomically, and Magnetically because the medicine is in them and the Magnet is in Man. This is because Will belongs to the category of **relational terms** <gloss>al-muḍāf</gloss>. It has been demonstrated that when one of two relational terms exists in act, the other must also exist in act, such as father and son; and if one exists in potential, the other exists in potential. Therefore, if the **Will in act** is created in time, the **object of will** <gloss>al-murād</gloss> must necessarily be created in time. But if the Will in act is eternal, then the object of will in act is also eternal.

As for the Will that precedes the object of will, that is **Will in potential** <gloss>al-irāda bi-l-quwwa</gloss>. By this, I mean a Will whose object has not yet moved into actuality because the action necessary for the occurrence of the object was not yet coupled with that Will. But the unlearned and those of a [base] nature—to whom, truly, the fate of obtaining gifts from the Lord did not come—neither have a notion of the immortal Jove <note>original: "Iovis"; used here by Porphyry to refer to the supreme deity</note>; nor do they listen to both gods and divine men. They have indeed rejected all gods, but as for the prohibited demons, they have chosen not only to follow them with no hatred, but even to revere them. While they pretend to worship God, they do not perform those things alone by which God is adored. For God, as the father of all, indeed stands in need of nothing; but it is well for us when we adore Him through justice and chastity and other virtues, making our very life a prayer to Him through the imitation and instruction concerning Him. For instruction purifies, he says, and imitation deifies by working the affection toward Him. Indeed, he [Porphyry] preached well about God the Father and said by what customs He is to be worshipped. The prophetic books of the Hebrews are full of these precepts, when the life of the saints is either praised or censured. But among the Christians there was only [error], or they are slandered only as much as the demons—whom they suppose to be gods—wish. As if it were difficult for anyone to recall what shameful and disgraceful things were performed in the service of the gods in theaters and temples, and to observe what is read, spoken, and heard in the churches, or what is offered to the true God; and from this to understand where there is a building up and where a ruin of morals. Who, moreover, told him this or inspired him, if not a diabolic spirit: such a vain and obvious lie, that the Christians revere the demons prohibited from being worshipped by the Hebrews, rather than hating them? But that God whom the wise men of the Hebrews worshipped—and the celestial holy angels and powers of God, whom we venerate and love as most blessed citizens in this our mortal pilgrimage—forbids sacrifice to be made [to others], thundering in His law which He gave to His Hebrew people; and He brought it in very threateningly, saying: He who sacrifices to gods shall be rooted out. And lest anyone should think that the command was not to sacrifice to the most wicked and earthly spirits, whom that man [Porphyry] calls the least or lesser ones—for in the holy scriptures these are also called gods, not of the Hebrews

<column-break/>

but of the gentiles—which the seventy interpreters <note>The Septuagint: the Greek translation of the Old Testament</note> placed clearly in the psalm, saying: For all the gods of the gentiles are demons. Therefore, lest anyone should think it was prohibited to sacrifice to these demons, but permitted to sacrifice to all or some of the celestial beings, He immediately added: except to the Lord alone; that is, except to the Lord only. Lest perhaps he who says "to the Lord alone" might believe that there is some other God to whom he thinks sacrifice should be made. That it is not to be understood this way is very easily found in the Greek scriptures. Therefore the God of the Hebrews, to whom even this great philosopher <note>Porphyry</note> bears such great testimony, gave the law to His Hebrew people, written in the Hebrew tongue—not obscure and unknown, but now spread abroad among all nations—in which law it is written: He who sacrifices to gods shall be rooted out, except to the Lord only. What need is there to search out many things in this His law and His prophets concerning this matter? Or rather, not to search for them? For they are not hidden or rare, but plain and frequent things to collect and place in this my discussion, by which it appears clearer than light that He, the true and supreme God, wished sacrifice to be made to none at all except only to Himself. Behold this one thing, spoken briefly, or rather grandly, threateningly, but truly by that God whom the most learned of them preach as so excellent: let it be heard, let it be feared, let it be fulfilled, lest the rooting out of the disobedient follow. He who sacrifices to gods shall be rooted out, He says, except to the Lord only. Not because He has need of anything, but because it is profitable for us that we should be His property. For to Him it is sung in the sacred letters of the Hebrews: I have said to the Lord, you are my God, since you have no need of my goods. Moreover, the most excellent and best sacrifice to Him is we ourselves. This is His City, the mystery of which we celebrate with our oblations, which are known to the faithful, as we have discussed in the preceding books. For the Hebrew prophets gave forth oracles that the victims which the Jews offered in the shadow of the future were to cease, and that the nations would offer one sacrifice from the rising of the sun even to its setting, just as we now see being done.

Has it not reached you how a raven destroyed a black snake?"

**Dimna** said: "They mention that a raven had a nest in a mountain, and near it was the hole of a black snake. The snake used to eat the raven’s chicks. He said to him: 'I want to go to the black snake and peck out its eyes while it is sleeping, so that perhaps I may be relieved of it.'

The <term>Terumah</term> <gloss>the Great Heave-offering given to the priest</gloss> and the <term>Bikkurim</term> <gloss>First Fruits</gloss>
are alike in that one is liable for the penalty of death <note>at the hands of Heaven, if eaten intentionally by a non-priest</note> and the payment of an added fifth <note>if eaten accidentally, the principal plus twenty percent must be repaid</note>.
They are both forbidden to <term>zarim</term> <gloss>non-priests/strangers to the priesthood</gloss>,
they are the property of the priest,
they are neutralized in a mixture of one hundred and one parts <note>if one part of the holy offering falls into one hundred parts of common food, the mixture is permitted to commoners</note>,
and they require the washing of hands and the setting of the sun <note>the priest must be ritually pure and must wait until nightfall after immersion to consume them</note>.
These rules apply to <term>Terumah</term> and <term>Bikkurim</term>,
which is not the case for the <term>Ma'aser</term> <gloss>Second Tithe</gloss>.

## Tractate Bikkurim Chapter 2 Mishnah 2
->2<-
There are rules that apply to the <term>Ma'aser</term> and the <term>Bikkurim</term> which do not apply to <term>Terumah</term>:
For the <term>Ma'aser</term> and the <term>Bikkurim</term> require being brought to the place <note>Jerusalem</note>,
they require the recitation of the confession <note>the formal declarations prescribed in the Torah for tithes and first fruits</note>, and they are forbidden to an <term>onen</term> <gloss>a person in the first day of mourning</gloss>;
Rabbi Shimon permits them to an <term>onen</term>.
And they are subject to the law of removal <term>bi'ur</term> <gloss>the periodic clearing of tithes from the home in the third and sixth years of the sabbatical cycle</gloss>.
Rabbi Shimon exempts them.
And any amount of them is forbidden to be eaten in Jerusalem <note>if they have become impure or if the proper rituals were not completed</note>,
and their produce <note>what grows from their seeds</note> is forbidden to be eaten in Jerusalem,
even to non-priests and to livestock.
Rabbi Shimon permits this.
These rules apply to <term>Ma'aser</term> and <term>Bikkurim</term>,
which is not the case for <term>Terumah</term>.

no way let it remain hidden that some of the expressions <note>referring to the prophecies and scriptures mentioned previously</note> appear as metaphors <gloss>seem to be metaphorical</gloss> to the masters of language. Now, out of a sense of honor and in accordance with your request, we mention it again in these pages, that perhaps it may lead those thirsty in the desert of distance to the bridge of nearness, and bring those wandering the wilderness of separation and parting to the cup of reunion; so that the clouds of error may be lifted and the world-illuminating sun of guidance may dawn from the horizon of the soul. In God is our trust, and from Him we seek help.

May there flow from this pen that which shall quicken the hearts of men, that they may arise as one from the slumber of their negligence, and inhale the sweetest fragrances of the leaves of Paradise from the Tree <note>original: *sidrah* — the Lote-tree, representing the Manifestation of God</note> which was planted in the garden of Divinity by the hands of power with the permission of God. To those possessed of knowledge, it is clear and evident that when the fire of the love of Jesus <note>original: *muḥabbat-i-‘īsavī*</note> burned away the veils of limitation and form, and His sovereignty was established outwardly to some extent, that Hidden Beauty <note>original: *jamāl-i-ghaybī* — a title for the Divine Manifestation</note> one day spoke of departure to some of His spiritual companions. Kindling the fire of longing, He said: I go and I come again. On another day He said: I go, and another comes to say what I have not said, and to complete that which I have spoken. ### Chapter on the different groups among them, their doctrines, their signs, their stations, and their stories.

### **Torah** is Light. These commandments mentioned in this Torah portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Divine Service, and Acts of Loving-kindness <note>Mishnah Pirkei Avot 1:2</note>. 

**Torah** consists of the prohibitions "You shall not add" and "You shall not diminish," which indicate the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers have said: regarding a thing that is complete in ultimate perfection, one cannot say it is lacking or excessive. For if it were lacking, it would not be complete, and if it could accept an addition, it would mean it was not previously perfect. Therefore, the definition of "perfect" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is suspended upon His Great Name, which is <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term> <gloss>The Tetragrammaton</gloss>, for "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my work on Tractate Shevuot in the chapter "Torah Ohr." This is also stated in the Zohar regarding the verse "This is My name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: The letters <term>Yod-He</term> with "My name" <note>Hebrew: <term>Shemi</term></note> sum to 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>; the letters <term>Vav-He</term> with "My memorial" <note>Hebrew: <term>Zichri</term></note> sum to 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. And it is written, "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>—He is the Absolute Perfection, having neither deficiency nor addition. Regarding this comes the warning, "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, which is a warning against erasing the Name or breaking a stone from the Holy Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are like the house in which He, may He be blessed, dwells; so too is the Sanctuary. It is written, "I am the Lord, that is My name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>—the letters are like a lock for the house, and His Name, may He be blessed, is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God."

**Service** <note>Hebrew: <term>Avodah</term>, referring to sacrificial worship</note> comprises most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came for there to be a fixed place, in the Chosen House, and the verse provides the reason: "To His habitation shall you seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" alludes to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the Palace of the Name <term>Yod-He-Vav-He</term>. As it is written: "Do not fear, for she dwells within me," for in the Sanctuary, the Glory <note>Hebrew: <term>Kavod</term>, referring to the Sefirah of Malkhut</note> is unified with the Beauty <note>Hebrew: <term>Tiferet</term></note> of His people. This is the meaning of "to put His name there," which the Targum <gloss>Aramaic translation</gloss> renders as "to cause His Presence to dwell." Around the place of holiness "the wicked walk on every side" <note>Psalm 12:9</note>, representing the <term>Kelipot</term> <gloss>Husks/Forces of impurity</gloss>. Therefore: "Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes** sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inside. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn sacrifices from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written of them, "There you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have an ascent <note>A pun on <term>olah</term>, burnt offering/ascent</note>, and not outside. Since the holiness resides in the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, we are commanded to "turn from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret of this alludes to the ten nations whose power is not from idol worship <unclear>…</unclear>. The matter is that nations in the Land of Israel, being under the governance of the Honorable Name, worship God through "cutting the plantings" <note>A metaphor for heresy/dualism</note>, and this is actual idolatry. However, outside the Land, they are under the governance of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against breaking even one stone of holiness, conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate an Apostate City <note>Hebrew: <term>Ir HaNidachat</term></note> and never to rebuild it, for its place is impure. So too with the Enticer and Seducer <note>Hebrew: <term>Mesit u-Madiach</term></note>—one must uproot and eradicate him, for he stems from the impurity of the Primordial Serpent who was an enticer. The Holy One immediately said, "Cursed is the serpent," therefore the powers of <term>Samael</term> <gloss>the Angel of Evil</gloss> are never healed. The command came not to love him and not to listen to him, similar to what was said of the serpent: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman." A false prophet is also like an enticer. Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the First Fruits <note>Hebrew: <term>Bikkurim</term></note>, which the priests have no permission to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the First Fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness. Therefore, they must go to the holy place and from there receive their wisdom, for they are "holy to their God," and they shall eat in Jerusalem. The secret of Lesser Sanctity <note>Hebrew: <term>Kodashim Kalim</term></note> and the Second Tithe is that they are eaten in Jerusalem; this is the blessing of "grain, wine, and oil," which are the "fathers of fathers" of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat Lesser Sanctity until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul <note>Hebrew: <term>Nefesh</term></note>, and afterward permission is given to the body to enjoy. Know that just as the Service—the sacrifice—is an offering to God, so too is the worshiper. For the essence of the Service is that one sacrifices himself, in the secret of "When a man <note>Hebrew: <term>Adam</term></note> of you brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt offering is "entirely consumed," for it comes to atone for the thoughts of the heart <note>Hebrew: <term>Hirhur</term></note>, which are spiritual. It is burned all night so the serpent cannot hinder it. Lesser Sanctity represents the peace of the soul and the body.

### **The secret** of the firstborn is the secret of the "Holy Israel," who are called "Israel My firstborn" <note>Exodus 4:22</note>. He has compassion on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, the firstborn is eaten only by the priests. The secret of eating consecrated items corresponds to the blemished ones <unclear>…</unclear> for Israel is holy and Israel is called "Man" <note>Hebrew: <term>Adam</term></note>. This was the state of original holiness, but afterward a blemish fell upon him when he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin," yet he has a redemption through the secret of "And I will give a man in your stead." This was the secret of the <term>Azazel</term> <gloss>scapegoat</gloss>, who "carries their iniquities," meaning the iniquities that fall upon its head and its people. However, we are commanded not to intentionally cause a blemish in a consecrated animal in order to eat it. For if one casts a blemish in holy things by choice, it is a grave sin. So too the prohibition of labor and shearing with holy things, for even the "broken tablets" <note>The first set of Ten Commandments broken by Moses</note> remain holy.

### **The general principle** that emerges is that the Service is the sacrifice, but the internal sacrifice is Man. So too his soul is called to the Altar Above after his death, and Michael is the High Priest. This is the secret, for "in the image of God was Man made." Therefore, the warning was given to be careful with human life and not to kill a person except after thorough searching and inquiry. Then he is executed by the hand of Heaven, in the secret of "He is the Witness, He is the Judge," for the Lord is the True Witness and True Judge. So too the Sanhedrin must be like Him: just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean that they must verify the truth of the witnesses with complete clarity through searching and inquiry; then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven. "Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death [of His pious ones]" <note>Psalm 116:15</note>.

### **And since** the death of the pious is precious to God—for Israel is holy from the side of their soul, which after death cleaves to the heights—the command was given: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness..." for "You are children to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note>. This is not the case with the other nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, which is fitting since upon their death they go to perdition and have no portion in this world or the World to Come. We, however, are children of God. When we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, we instead have a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or perform these acts.

### **Let us return** to the matter: the man who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it is written, "When a man of you brings an offering." There is a further secret in this: Man is sometimes reincarnated even into an animal, in the secret of "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even regarding the eating of non-consecrated meat <note>Hebrew: <term>Basar Ta'avah</term></note>, we were commanded regarding ritual slaughter <note>Hebrew: <term>Shechitah</term></note> with great care, without any nick in the blade. For if there is a nick, it becomes a carcass <note>Hebrew: <term>Neveilah</term></note>, and then "a carcass is made in Israel." For who knows what soul is reincarnated within it? "Love your fellow as yourself"—choose for him a proper death, namely, slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies of its own, the power of impurity takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it properly, and the animal or pure bird contains a spark of holiness, then its soul departs in purity.

### **One who eats** a limb from a living animal <note>Hebrew: <term>Ever Min HaChay</term></note> is like one who eats human flesh when a reincarnated soul is present. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the spark spreading within them—whether it is from the Side of Impurity <note>Hebrew: <term>Sitra Achra</term></note> or the Side of Holiness <note>Hebrew: <term>Sitra de-Kedusha</term></note>. I elaborated on this in Parashat Shemini. When Israel conducts themselves with holiness, it is written of them: "And they shall make for Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>. For they themselves are the Tabernacle. Man is divided into three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies; the heart to the Holy Place; and from the belly downward to the Courtyard of the Sanctuary, as I elaborated in Parashat Terumah. When one eats foods from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Now, a man's table atones for him" <note>Talmud, Menachot 97a</note>, as I have elaborated elsewhere.

### **The matter** of the festival commandments and their sacrifices I have written about, each in its specific place. The command was given to rejoice on the festivals, to ascend on the pilgrimage, and "three times a year shall all your males appear." Just as one comes to see, so one comes to be seen. Therefore, if one wishes to be seen in the Holy Temple where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Otherwise, it is forbidden for a wicked person to enter the hall—how could he wish to be seen before Him and bring a burnt offering of appearance? Then he himself is the sacrifice through the animal he offers. It says "three times a year he shall appear"—alluding to Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering" <unclear>…</unclear>.

### On the shame sought from unworthy praise.
## DIALOGUE XXVI.

> Praise sparingly, for when you praise unjustly,
> If you later condemn, it will be a mark of levity.

# On the Motion of the Heart, etc.

Since these things are so, it is established that another point I stated before will also be confirmed: that blood passes continuously through the heart. For we see in the constitution of the body that blood flows from the arteries into the veins, not from the veins into the arteries. We see, moreover, that almost the entire mass of blood can be drained from the arm itself <note>specifically through a single superficial vein opened with a scalpel, provided a proper ligature is applied</note>. We further see it poured out so forcefully and abundantly that not only is the blood which was contained in the arm below the ligature before the incision evacuated quickly and shortly, but it is clear that blood is drawn from the whole arm and the whole body, from the arteries as well as the veins.

Therefore, it must first be acknowledged that blood is supplied by force and impulse, and is driven by force <note>original: "impingi"</note>

# Zechariah

And the angel answered and said to me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one in which are the black horses goes out to the north country, and the white ones go out after them, and the dappled ones go out to the south country. And the strong ones went out and sought to go, to walk about the earth; and he said, 'Go, walk about the earth.' And they walked about the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying, 'See, those who go out to the north country have given rest to my spirit in the north country.'"

**And the angel answered.** "These are the four winds." This is like "to the four winds." And so, "And he came to Jerusalem" <note>original: "va-yavo Yerushalayim"</note> is like "to Jerusalem." Another explanation: "white, black" is like "a white one and a black one," and similar examples. He divided the four chariots as going out to the four winds of the heavens. This means giving permission to the kingdoms to rule in the four winds, each one in its time. This refers to the whole world, which is the meaning of "strength." "From standing before the Lord of all the earth": this means by the mission of God who gave them power over this. It is like "The sons of God came to stand before the Lord" <margin>Job 2</margin>.

**The one in which.** "The black ones." He mentioned the black ones because the time of the Babylonian kingdom had already passed. The kingdom of Media and Persia would first go out to the north country, as they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. "And the white ones," which refers to the kingdom of Greece <note>original: "Yavan"</note>, "went out after them" because that kingdom was swift. Alexander of Macedon <term>Alexandros Maqedon</term>, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingship from him and reigned; and afterward his successors ruled throughout the whole world.

**And the dappled ones go out to the south country.** These were a hint to the kingdom of Rome, which is the Edomite kingdom. Julius Caesar <term>Yulius Caesar</term>, who ruled over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece. At the start of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is in the south. At that time, the Greeks ruled in all those lands, and Julius Caesar overpowered them, transferred the kingdom from the Greeks, and restored it to the Romans.

**And the strong ones.** These are an allusion to the kingdom of Ishmael <note>the Islamic conquests</note>, who exerted themselves on their own to seek a kingdom, to have a place that would be their own. This is why it says, "And they sought to go, to walk about the earth."

**And he said.** Meaning, He gave them permission to walk about and conquer lands.

**Then he cried out.** Meaning, he called to me with a loud voice and said to me, **"See, those who go out to the north country have given rest to my spirit in the north country."** This refers to the portion of the black horses who went out to Babylon to destroy it.

The person undergoing evacuation <note>purging</note> must not rush into eating many heavy foods, for the <term>Tabi'ah</term> <gloss>Nature/innate constitution</gloss> would then attract them while they are still undigested. If such food is necessary, it must be taken little by little, spaced out so that it is gradual, ensuring that what enters the body is well-digested.

Bloodletting <note>original: <term>al-fasd</term></note> is the evacuation specifically for the blood in its balanced state. As for evacuation specific to a humor that has become excessive in quantity or corrupted in quality, it is something other than bloodletting. Every excessive evacuation usually causes vomiting. For someone whose habitual diarrhea has stopped, causing an ailment, the return of that evacuation usually cures it; for instance, if the cessation of a nosebleed or nasal discharge caused a blockage, its return will remove it.

Know that the remaining matter which needs evacuation is less able to withstand thorough purging <note>until completion</note> if it leads to the exhaustion of strength. Often, Nature itself dissolves those remains. As long as the humor is of the type intended for removal and the patient can bear it, do not fear excess; you may even need to evacuate until fainting <note>original: <term>al-ghashi</term></note>. For one whose strength is firm but whose bad humors are many, evacuate them little by little. Likewise, do it gradually if the matter is highly matured <note>original: <term>shadid al-nudj</term></note> or heavily mixed with the blood and cannot be evacuated all at once—as occurs in sciatica, chronic joint pains, cancer, chronic scabies, and chronic boils.

Know that diarrhea draws from above and uproots from below; it is suited to the accustomed drawing and also suited after the materials have settled. If the materials are below, diarrhea draws them to itself and uproots them from where they are. Vomiting acts by drawing in the opposite direction. The state of bloodletting varies according to the sites from which blood is taken, as you have learned. The people least in need of evacuation are those with good digestion, and those in hot countries have little need for evacuation.

### Chapter Four: On the Common Rules for Vomiting and Diarrhea and an Indication of How Laxative Drugs and Emetics Attract Humors

We say it is recommended for one who wishes to take a laxative to hold back or distribute his food firmly. First, the amount he usually takes in a day should be divided into portions, making them of different foods and different drinks. In this state, the stomach will desire to push what is in it either upwards or downwards. As for eating non-varied food—relying on a single type—the stomach becomes saturated by it, becomes sluggish, and grips it tightly, especially if it is small in quantity. For those with naturally soft bowels, none of this is necessary.

Know that the need for vomiting, diarrhea, and the like does not occur in one who follows a good regimen <note>original: <term>husn al-tadbir</term></note>; such a person needs only lighter measures. Perhaps exercise, massage, and cupping will suffice him for his ailments. If his body becomes filled—mostly with the best of humors, namely blood—then bloodletting is what is needed for its purification, rather than a laxative. 

If necessity dictates bloodletting or evacuation in a season like autumn, begin with vomiting then follow with bloodletting; this is among the counsels of Hippocrates <note>original: <term>Abiqrat</term></note> and the writings of Apollo, and it is the truth. Likewise, if phlegmatic humors are mixed with the blood. However, if the humors are equal but viscous and cold, bloodletting might increase their thickness and viscosity; in that case, one must begin with a laxative. In general, if the humors are equal, prioritize bloodletting; if an excess remains after that, then evacuate. If they are unequal, evacuate the excess first until they are balanced, then perform bloodletting.

If one prioritizes medicine over bloodletting, he should have performed the bloodletting a few days prior. If someone has recently undergone bloodletting and needs evacuation, drinking the medicine should be delayed for him. Often, drinking medicine when bloodletting was required results in vomiting and distress; if it does not settle with sedatives, then bloodletting should have preceded it. There is no evacuation required by excessive fullness <note>original: <term>al-imtila'</term></note> that is not dictated by the severity of the illness and the fullness in both quality and quantity.

Often, a good regimen makes the required bloodletting unnecessary at the time. Often, the cause calls for evacuation, but an obstacle arises, leaving no trick for it except fasting, sleep, and correcting the <term>su' mizaj</term> <gloss>distemper/mal-temperament</gloss> caused by the fullness. Some evacuation is performed as a precaution <note>original: <term>al-istizhar</term></note>, such as what is needed for those accustomed to gout, epilepsy, or other ailments at a known time, especially in the spring; one needs to take precautions before the time and perform the specific evacuation, whether bloodletting or a laxative. Sometimes the use of external drying agents and powders acts as an evacuation, as is done for those with dropsy.

You may need to use a medicine that matches the humor being evacuated in quality, such as scammony <note>original: <term>saqmuniya</term></note> when you need to evacuate yellow bile. In that case, you must mix it with something that opposes it in quality but aids it in purging, such as myrobalan <note>original: <term>al-halilaj</term></note>. If a distemper occurs afterward in those with tumors of the viscera, their purging becomes weak. If forced to do so, use for them things like bindweed or safflower.

Regarding the laxative and purging cassia <note>original: <term>khiyar shanbar</term></note>: Hippocrates said that for one whose constitution easily responds to vomiting, the first step in his purification is to use vomiting in the summer or spring, for that protects the body from exhaustion. Know that if the drinker has a "slippery" <note>irritable</note> stomach or is naturally loose-boweled, or is not accustomed to vomiting, he should avoid it unless necessary. 

One must thicken <note>the humor</note> before diarrhea and vomiting by thinning the humor intended for evacuation and widening the passages. Know that for one who is loose-boweled or unaccustomed to vomiting, using a strong medicine alongside thinness of the abdominal walls <note>original: <term>hazal al-maraqq</term></note> is difficult and exhausting. An emetic medicine may turn into a laxative if the stomach is strong, if it is drunk during intense hunger, if the drinker is loose-boweled, or if the medicine is heavier in substance than those that descend quickly. Conversely, a laxative may become an emetic due to weakness of the stomach, extreme heaviness, or if the medicine is repulsive to the patient and he suffers from indigestion. 

Every laxative drug, if it does not purge due to lack of maturation, will stir up the humor it was meant to purge and spread it through the body. It then overcomes the body and draws other humors toward it, increasing that humor in the body. Some humors respond more quickly to vomiting, like yellow bile, while others resist it, like black bile. Some have a specific state, like phlegm; purging it <note>downwards</note> is more correct in itself. 

For one whose humor is already descending, such as those with "slipping of the intestines" <note>original: <term>zalaq al-am'a'</term>, likely lientery or chronic diarrhea</note>, the intestines grip, and laxative medicines made of highly different ingredients become difficult during the time of purging, causing distress; the first part may purge the second before the second can act. If someone undergoes purging while their body is clean, they cannot avoid the medicine causing colic and distress, and the evacuation will be very difficult. In general, when medicine evacuates waste, there is no distress; if it is taken with distress, it is either evacuating something other than waste, or the humor being evacuated has changed during the vomiting or diarrhea to another humor, indicating that the body has been cleansed of the intended humor.

They descend into the status of impurity through intent, but they do not ascend <note>meaning they do not lose their status of impurity</note> except through a physical act. A physical act removes an object from the status of a prior act or prior intent, but intent does not remove an object from the status of an act or even from prior intent. And if we say that they are for the purpose of eating, then through intent they should become <note>susceptible to impurity</note> and through intent that status should be removed. But did we not learn in a Mishnah: * All "handles" of food items <note>stalks or attachments</note> that are in the <term>siman</term> <gloss>bundle/stack</gloss> on the threshing floor are pure <note>not susceptible to impurity</note>, and Rabbi Yose declares them impure. It is understandable according to the one who says <term>besiman</term> means they are bundled together, but according to the one who says what is <term>besiman</term>? It means literally in the storehouse, what can be said? Here too, it means literally in the storehouse. If so, what is the reason of the Rabbis? For they speak according to Rabbi Yose, as we learned: * Rabbi Yose declares them impure. But granted there, the reason of Rabbi Yose is according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Since they are fit to be turned over with a pitchfork <note>the stalk serves as a handle for the tool</note>. But here, what are they fit for? It can be said: for catching them by their husks. As for the matter itself: All handles of food items in the bundle on the threshing floor are pure, and Rabbi Yose and Shimon ben Lakish. What is <term>besiman</term>? Rabbi Yohanan said: Literally in the bundle. Rabbi Eleazar says: It means the pitchfork of the bundle. Since Rabbi Eleazar says the pitchfork of the bundle, that is why Rabbi Yose declares it impure. Rather, Rabbi Eleazar, why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork <note>term: eter</note>? To tell you: Just as this pitchfork turns the grain on the threshing floor from place to place, so the prayer of the righteous turns the mind of the Holy One, Blessed be He, from the attribute of cruelty to the attribute of mercy.

And so, after foreign nations were harassed and ruined as an example, we saw the city of Marseilles <note>original: Massilia; a city that sided with Pompey against Caesar and was subsequently besieged and stripped of its wealth</note> carried in a triumphal procession; we saw a triumph celebrated over that very city, without which our generals never celebrated a triumph for wars beyond the Alps. I could mention many other wicked acts against our allies, if the sun had ever seen anything more unworthy than this one case. We are therefore punished with justice. For unless we had tolerated their crimes without punishment, such unbridled license would never have reached a single man. From him, the inheritance of private property came to a few, but the inheritance of his ambition came to many wicked men. Nor, indeed, will the seed and cause of civil wars ever be absent, as long as desperate men remember that bloody spear and hope for it. When Lucius Sulla brandished it while his kinsman was dictator, thirty-six years later he did not shrink from an even more wicked spear. Another man, however, who had been a clerk in that earlier dictatorship, was the city quaestor <note>an official in charge of the treasury</note> in this later one. From this, it must be understood that as long as such rewards are offered, there will never be an end to civil wars. Therefore, only the walls of the city stand and remain, and even these now fear the most extreme crimes; but we have truly lost the Republic entirely. And we have fallen into these disasters. ### Question

#### Article 3. Whether more universal things are prior in our intellectual cognition.

Regarding the third point, we proceed as follows. It seems that more universal things are not prior in our intellectual cognition. First, because those things which are prior and better known according to nature are posterior and less known according to us; but universals are prior according to the nature of our intellect. Furthermore, composites are prior for us compared to simple things; but universals are simpler, therefore they are known later by us. Furthermore, the Philosopher <note>Aristotle</note> says in the first book of the *Physics* that the thing defined first falls into our cognition, and the parts of the definition are less universal: just as "animal" is a part of the definition of "man," and thus universals are known later by us. Furthermore, we arrive at effects by chance and at principles. However, universals are known later by us. 

But there is that which is said in the first book of the *Physics*, that from universals one must arrive at singulars.

I respond that it must be said that in the cognition of our intellect, two things must be considered. First, indeed, that intellectual cognition in some way takes its beginning from sensitive cognition. And because the sense is of singulars and the intellect is of universals, it is necessary that the cognition of singulars, for us, be prior to the cognition of universals. Second, we must consider that our intellect proceeds from potentiality to act. And what proceeds from potentiality into act first reaches an incomplete act, which is midway between potentiality and act, and then a perfect act. The perfect act to which the intellect arrives is complete science through which things are known distinctly and determinately; the incomplete act is imperfect science through which things are known indistinctly under a certain confusion. For what is known in this way is known both in act and in a certain way in potentiality. As the Philosopher says in the first book of the *Physics*: things that are more confused are first manifest and certain to us. Later, however, we know by distinguishing the principles and elements distinctly. 

It is manifest, moreover, that to know something in which many things are contained without having proper knowledge of each of those things contained in it, is to know something under a certain confusion. In this way, both the whole in which parts are contained in potentiality and the integral whole can be known; for either whole can be known in a certain confusion without the parts being distinctly known. To know distinctly that which is contained in the whole is to have cognition of a less common thing: just as knowing "animal" indistinctly is knowing "animal" as it is, whereas knowing it with being rational or irrational is to know "man" or "horse." Therefore, it first occurs to our intellect to know "animal" rather than to know "man." And the same reasoning holds if we compare anything more universal to the less universal. Since sense goes out from potentiality into act, so does the intellect: and this order

<column-break/>

of cognition appears in the senses. For we judge more by sense when a thing is seen more remotely, as it is perceived to be a body; and then it is perceived to be an animal; and later it is perceived to be a man; and finally it is perceived to be Socrates. Or as is clear in the case of a child, who from the beginning first distinguishes a man from a non-man; and children from the beginning call all men "fathers." Later, however, they determine each one specifically, as is said in the first book of the *Physics*. It is manifest that someone who knows something indistinctly is still in potentiality, whereas knowing the genus is potential until one knows the differences. And thus, in itself, indistinct cognition is midway between potentiality and act. And thus the cognition of singulars is prior for us in sensitive cognition, but universal cognition is prior in intellectual cognition. If we compare sense with intellect, the more universal cognition is prior to the less universal and common.

To the first, it must be said that "prior" can be considered in two ways. In one way, as it is considered according to the intention of truth. And since the intention of truth is that the true and the same have a relationship to many, it follows that the abstraction of the intellect is the end in this way, while in truth it is posterior. In the first book of *On the Soul* <note>Aristotle's De Anima</note>, it is said that the universal is either nothing or it is posterior. But Plato placed universals as substances; and in this consideration it is true, because particulars are not unless by participation in more universal subsisting things which are called Ideas. 

In another way, it can be considered regarding the nature itself of "animality" or "humanity" as it is found in particulars. And thus there is a double order of nature. One according to the way of generation and time, since in that way things that are imperfect and in potentiality are prior. And in this way, the more universal is prior in nature, as is clearly seen in the generation of man and animal. For "animal" is generated before "man," as is said in the book *On the Generation of Animals*. The other is the order of perfection or the intention of nature, just as act is simply prior in nature, and the perfect is prior to the imperfect; and in this way the less universal is prior in nature, as "man" is to "animal." For the intention of nature does not stop at the generation of an animal, but intends to generate a man.

To the second, it must be said that the more universal is compared to the less universal as a whole, because the more universal contains in itself not only "man" and "horse" but others as well. Thus "animal" considered in itself is prior in our cognition to "man." If "man" were prior in our cognition to "animal," it would be through his specific reasoning.

To the third, it must be said that something can be known in two ways. In one way, absolutely according to what it is in itself, and thus nothing is known. In another way, as it is a part of this whole; just as with stones, it is necessary that we first know the whole before the parts. For we first know the house in a certain confused way. Thus it must be said that the defining parts, considered absolutely, are prior to us than the defined. Otherwise the defined would not be made known through them. But they are rather parts of the whole.

<summary>Thomas Aquinas discusses the order of human knowledge, arguing that intellectual cognition proceeds from the more universal and confused to the specific and distinct. He reconciles this with Aristotle's Physics, explaining that while singulars are known first by the senses, the intellect first grasps broad, universal concepts before refining them into specific definitions.</summary>

When the Lion woke on the following day, the Judge and a group of his noble companions entered his presence with a written record of what Dimna had said in his defense <term>ma'adhirihi</term> <gloss>his excuses or justifications</gloss>. The Lion took the record and ordered them to depart from him.

Then he sent for his mother and read the record to her. It distressed her, and she said: "If I am harsh with you, O King, do not be angry."

The Lion said: "I will not be angry, so say what you wish."

She said: "I do not see you recognizing what harms you from what benefits you. I believe that by prolonging your consideration of Dimna's case, he will stir up against you a situation that you will neither be able to withstand nor overcome."

Then she stood and left in a state of anger. When the next day came, the Judge sent for Dimna and brought him out. He consulted the scholars <term>al-ulama</term> regarding him, but they said nothing.

The Judge said to him: "Even if all those present remain silent and say nothing, their suspicions have united in the belief that you are a criminal. There is no good for you in life after the accusation has settled in their hearts. I see nothing better for you than to confess your sin, so that you might save your neck from the consequences of the Afterlife, and that a good word may return to your reputation for two reasons. The first is your power in finding ways out and fabricating excuses <note>original: "al-ma'adhir"</note> to defend yourself, and the second is your voluntary confession of your sin, choosing peace in the Afterlife over peace in this world. For the scholars have said: Death in what is beautiful is better than life in what is ugly."

Dimna answered him, saying: "Judges do not rule based on their own suspicions, nor on the suspicions of the common people or the elite. I have learned that suspicion is no substitute for the truth. Even if you all suspect that I am the author of this crime, I know myself best, and my knowledge of myself is a certainty without doubt. My case has only become ugly in your souls—if that is indeed the case—because you suspected that I acted with malice."

The state of the <term>Sheikh</term> <gloss>religious elder</gloss>, the <term>Qazi</term> <gloss>judge</gloss>, and their secret drinking <note>original: "shurb al-yahudan," literally "drinking like the Jews," implying clandestine drinking to avoid public scandal</note>,
I asked of the old wine-seller at the break of dawn.

He said, "These matters are not to be spoken of, even though you are a confidant;
Draw back your tongue, maintain the veil of secrecy, and drink your wine."

<term>Saqi</term> <gloss>wine-bearer</gloss>, spring is arriving and the means for wine is gone;
Think of something, for the heart’s blood boils over with grief.

Your love, my poverty, my youth, and the new spring—
Accept my excuse and cover my fault with the hem of your generosity.

How long will you display your eloquence like a guttering candle?
The butterfly of your desire has arrived; O lover, be silent.

O King of form and meaning, the likes of whom
No eye has ever seen and no ear has ever heard;

Remain so long that your youthful fortune
May accept the blue cloak from the aged sky <note>original: "khirqa-ye azraq," a reference to the blue garments of Sufis, here suggesting the sky itself honors the King</note>.

Last night, a sharp-witted man of skill spoke to me in secret,
For from the wine-seller, nothing should be hidden:

He said, "Take things easily upon yourself, for by its very nature,
The world treats those who strive too hard with great severity."

And then he gave me a cup from whose radiance in the heavens,
Venus began to dance and the lute-player <note>the constellation Lyra</note> covered its ears in wonder.

Bring a smiling lip even with a bleeding heart, like the wine-cup;
Do not cry out like the wailing harp if you receive a wound.

Until you become an initiate, you shall not hear a mystery from behind this veil;
The ear of the stranger is no place for the message of <term>Soroush</term> <gloss>the herald angel</gloss>.

When the boundless army became a massive throng,
He sought the tally of the illustrious names.

Gilded, elite horsemen had come forth.
When the preparation of the army was complete,
He held a gathering outside with the wine-cup.
The wise minds of Rome sat together;

# The Nahidiyah Maqama

Isa ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying:
I turned with a group of my companions to the courtyard of a tent, seeking hospitality from its folk. A scorched-looking man <note>darkened by the sun</note> came out to us and said: "Who are you?" We said: "Guests who have not tasted an enemy <note>meaning food, as a play on words</note> for three days." 

He said: "Step aside." Then he said: "O youths, what think you of a bowl of <term>nahidah</term> <gloss>a dish of butter and flour</gloss>, trembling like the crown of a bald man’s head, in a wide basin, crowned with a choice froth from the sides of a great, resting camel? One scoop of it fills the mouth of a group of hungry, thirsty men; the tooth vanishes into it as if its pits were birds' tongues. They scoop up the <term>nahidah</term> with bowls filled with milk milked from sturdy, aged, well-fed camels. Do you desire it, O youths?" 

We said: "By God, yes, we desire it!" 

The old man guffawed and said: "And your uncle <note>referring to himself</note> also desires it!" Then he said: "What is your opinion, O youths, of fine white bread <note>original: "darmak"</note>, like pieces of silver ingots, arranged on a leather mat smelling of mimosa bark? A bright, clever, nimble youth leaps to it and kneads it without shaking or rattling it, making it smoother than a soft angel. Then he moistens it with water or a pestle, making it thick. Then he turns to it, twists it, and leaves it in the corner of a <term>Saida</term> <gloss>a type of stone or oven</gloss> until it rises without becoming hard. He heads for the <term>ghada</term> wood and kindles the fire. When its flame dies down, he prepares its bed of hot ashes, then takes his dough and throws it in after perfecting its color. He spreads it out, covers it, and when it bubbles and pits, he heaps upon it hot stones until the two heats meet. When he covers them on the matching embers with a lid, it cracks open into thin layers, its crust mimicking the thinness and redness of the famous Hijazi dates known as 'Mother of Locusts' or 'Adaq ibn Tab'. He then sprinkles upon it something white as snow <note>sugar or fat</note> until it sinks into the folds of the grease, and the heart of the bread drinks what is upon it. I present it to you and you swallow it in great gulps. Do you desire it, O youths?"

He said: We all craned our necks at his description, our mouths watering and our lips smacking. We said: "By God, yes, we desire it!" 

He said: The old man guffawed and said: "And your uncle, by God, does not hate it!" Then he said: "What is your opinion, O youths, of a young she-goat from Najd, high-bred and wild, that has eaten the mimosa blossoms, the Najdi wormwood, the yarrow, and the dry herbage? She has sipped the summer rain and filled herself with the lush grass until her sides are bursting. She is then slaughtered in joy and inverted in a pit-oven <note>original: "watis"</note> until she is cooked through without being scorched or underdone. Then we present her to you, her skin covering white fat, on a table arranged with thin loaves like spreading fine Egyptian linen or dyed cloth. She is surrounded by dips and various finger-foods, placed before you dripping with juice and oozing gravy. Do you desire it, O youths?" 

We said: "By God, yes, we desire it!" 

He said: "And your uncle, by God, dances for it!" 

At this, one of us leapt at him with a sword and said: "What..."

At this time, we saw ourselves as worthy of producing a work to be transmitted after us. It became incumbent upon us that you should be the first person we present with our findings and inform of what we possess, due to the soundness of your loyalty and the purity of your friendship. However, if we were to cast upon you the ultimate conclusions of what we have reached without first establishing the principles with you, it would benefit you in no way beyond a mere general imitation. This would only be the case if you thought well of us based on our friendship and familiarity, rather than believing that our words deserve acceptance on their own merit. 

We do not desire for you anything less than the highest rank. We are not satisfied with this level of imitation for you, as it does not guarantee salvation, let alone the attainment of the highest degrees of success. Rather, we wish to lead you along the same paths that we have already traveled, and to swim with you in the sea that we crossed first, until it brings you to the same end we reached. Then you may witness what we witnessed, verify with your own inner sight everything we verified, and be free from binding your knowledge to what we have known. 

This journey requires a specific and significant amount of time, freedom from distractions, and the devotion of one's entire will to this art. If your resolve is sincere and your intention to prepare yourself for this quest is sound, then at morning you will praise your nocturnal journey <note>A traditional Arabic proverb meaning that the hard work of the night is rewarded by the success found at daybreak</note> and you will receive the blessing of your efforts. You will have pleased your Lord, and He will have pleased you. I am at your service to help you reach what you desire and what you aspire to with your full determination and being. I hope to lead you along the most direct path, safest from dangers and pitfalls. Now, I will present a brief glimpse into
